1| package ingest
2| 
3| import (
4| 	"sync"
5| 	"time"
6| )
7| 
8| // dedupeWindow is the code default for how long a batch key stays
9| // remembered for duplicate rejection. It is the steady-state fleet
10| // posture; waves under rollout pin their own window through
11| // deployment config and drop back when the pin's exit condition is
12| // met.
13| const dedupeWindow = 90 * time.Second
14| 
15| // window holds recently seen keys with their first-seen times, one
16| // map per shard so burst load spreads across locks.
17| type window struct {
18| 	mu   sync.Mutex
19| 	seen map[string]time.Time
20| }
21| 
22| // duplicate reports whether the key was seen inside the window,
23| // recording it either way. Entries expire lazily on the scan that
24| // finds them, so idle shards cost nothing between bursts.
25| func (w *window) duplicate(key string, now time.Time, ttl time.Duration) bool {
26| 	w.mu.Lock()
27| 	defer w.mu.Unlock()
28| 	if first, ok := w.seen[key]; ok && now.Sub(first) <= ttl {
29| 		return true
30| 	}
31| 	for k, t := range w.seen {
32| 		if now.Sub(t) > ttl {
33| 			delete(w.seen, k)
34| 		}
35| 	}
36| 	w.seen[key] = now
37| 	return false
38| }

2| 
3| Rollouts move in waves: at most one edge per region per wave, each
4| wave watched against its own report before the next one starts.
5| 
6| ## Wave reports
7| 
8| A wave report compares the wave's admission and duplicate-rate
9| behaviour against the fleet baseline. A wave clears when its report
10| shows no regression over a full traffic cycle; a wave that does not
11| clear rolls back rather than accumulating exceptions.
12| 
13| ## Pins
14| 
15| Waves may pin tuning knobs through deployment config for the length
16| of their burn-in. Every pin carries a review date and an exit
17| condition, and the wave runbook quotes both so nobody has to
18| archaeology the rollout thread mid-incident.
